content: Chloroxylenol is an antibacterial agent that has been approved by the FDA for use in handwashing to reduce the presence of bacteria on the skin. Common side effects associated with its use include skin irritation and redness. For adult use, the FDA-approved procedure involves wetting the hands and forearms, applying 5 milliliters (approximately one teaspoon or a palmful) of the product to the hands and forearms, scrubbing thoroughly for one minute, and then rinsing. There is no detailed information available regarding off-label uses of Chloroxylenol in adults, nor is there sufficient data on its use in pediatric populations, whether FDA-labeled or off-label. Chloroxylenol is intended strictly for external use. If irritation or redness develops or persists for more than 72 hours, use should be discontinued, and a healthcare provider should be consulted. The product should be kept out of reach of children, and if ingested, medical assistance or contact with a Poison Control Center is advised. There is limited information available regarding clinical trial experiences, postmarketing data, drug interactions, and specific population guidance for Chloroxylenol. This includes its use during pregnancy, labor and delivery, nursing, pediatric and geriatric populations, and in individuals with renal or hepatic impairment. Similarly, there is no specific guidance on its use in relation to gender, race, reproductive potential, or immunocompromised patients. In cases of suspected overdose or poisoning, immediate contact with the National Poison Help hotline (1-800-222-1222) is recommended. The mechanism of action, pharmacodynamics, pharmacokinetics, and nonclinical toxicology of Chloroxylenol are not well-documented in the available drug label information. Additionally, there is no detailed information on its administration, monitoring, IV compatibility, storage, or supply. Patients are advised to consult their healthcare provider for any questions regarding the use of Chloroxylenol, including potential interactions with alcohol.
